title: Consolidated Fidelity Governance Blueprint
author: Aisha Patel
body:
Overview

This blueprint defines a consolidated governance and commercialization approach for output "fidelity" across Redwood’s product surface (Hosted API, Dedicated, Private, and Optimize). It describes principles, roles, product requirements, design constraints, a cross-functional rollout roadmap, pricing/packaging implications, telemetry and quality gates, and a phased release and experiment plan. This doc is intended for PMs, product engineering, applied ML, finance, and sales leadership.

Goals and motivation

1. Make fidelity a first-class product primitive: expose clear levers (fidelity tiers, fallback variants, quantization switches, latency tiers) that customers can reason about and adopt.
2. Align SLAs, pricing, and operational controls so fidelity transitions are predictable for customers and profitable for Redwood.
3. Provide governance that prevents quality regressions while enabling rapid experimentation (A/B, canary) across customers.

Scope

- Surface areas: Hosted API, Redwood Dedicated, Redwood Private, Redwood Optimize advisor and conductor.
- Fidelity controls included: model variant selection, token-budgeting, quantization profiles, batching/caching fidelity knobs, streaming fidelity negotiation.
- Not in scope: model training fidelity, open-source-model licensing constraints (handled by model-onboarding).

Principles

- Observable: every fidelity change must be instrumented with cost, latency, and quality metrics mapped to prompt-sets.
- Reversible and safe: rollouts must include automatic rollback triggers tied to loss/quality regressions or cost thresholds.
- Commercially explicit: customers know which fidelity tier maps to consumption rates and pricing credits.
- Unified: same governance primitives across hosted, dedicated, and private where feasible.

Governance model (high level)

- Product Council (monthly): PMs from Hosting, Dedicated, Optimize + Applied ML + Finance + Sales. Approves fidelity tier definitions, pricing deltas, and major rollout windows. Owner: product.
- Technical Review Board (bi-weekly): engineering leads from serving runtime, infra, and SRE review operational constraints, rollout automation, and safety checks. Owner: engineering.
- Experiment Review: ad-hoc sign-off for cross-customer experiments that affect fidelity defaults or fallback policies. Owner: applied ML.

Roles & responsibilities

- Product (owner): define tier definitions, customer-facing UX/Docs, commercial mapping.
- Applied ML: quality metrics, prompt-set maintenance, acceptance gates for quantized/low-fidelity variants.
- Eng (Serving Runtime): implement fallback/negotiation hooks, rollout flags, performance profiles.
- Eng (SRE/Platform): SLOs, alerts, capacity planning for staged rollouts.
- Finance & GTM: pricing CAD/negotiation guidance, revenue/regression modeling for tier changes.

Key SLOs and thresholds

- Fidelity-guarded quality SLOs: 
  - Regression signal: average rouge-like fidelity score delta across canonical prompt-sets <= 2% per rollout window.
  - Latency SLO by tier: P95 <= 300ms (premium), P95 <= 700ms (standard), P95 <= 1.5s (economy).
  - Availability SLO: 99.9% for hosted premium endpoints; 99.5% for economy.
- Cost signal thresholds (relative to baseline variant): upgrade if cost delta <= +12% for equivalent quality; fallback/rollback if delta >= +30% or if customer spend predictability is violated.

Product requirements (PRD-style)

1) Fidelity Tier Definition API & UX
- Expose named tiers: premium, standard, economy, and adaptive. Each tier includes: model variant set, max tokens-per-request, quantization profile, batching policy, fallback policy.
- UI: per-route fidelity selector in Console with clear cost delta and latency estimate.
- API: per-request header and route-level default for fidelity.

2) Rollout/Experiment Framework
- Canary targets: tenant-level targeting, % traffic, and duration parameters.
- Automatic rollback triggers: quality delta > threshold, cost delta breach, or error-rate increase > 2x baseline.
- Data capture: aligned eval captures (input, reference, model output hash) stored to secure retention.

3) Billing & Commercial Mapping
- Each fidelity tier maps to a multiplier applied to base token consumption (e.g., premium x1.0, standard x0.85, economy x0.6). Multipliers must be configurable per contract.
- Credits reconciliation: fidelity downgrades/upgrades across billing periods must be prorated.

4) Observability & Quality Gates
- Per-route fidelity dashboards: token-cost, p50/p95 latency, quality delta vs baseline prompt-sets, fallback counts.
- Alerting: fidelity-regression PagerDuty channel with severity tiers (SEV3: early warning; SEV2: rollback recommended; SEV1: automatic rollback executed).

Design constraints and non-goals

- Design for multi-tenant safety: avoid noisy-neighbor effects from aggressive batching when a tenant is in premium tier.
- Where runtime differences between Dedicated and Hosted make exact parity impossible, define explicit compatibility matrices and documented fallback behavior.
- Non-goal: providing per-customer bespoke fidelity models outside variant marketplace (handled by enterprise professional services).

Operational rollout plan (phases)

Phase 0 — Preparation (Q4 2026)
- Finalize tier definitions and acceptance prompt-set.
- Implement telemetry panels and acceptance pipelines.
- Finance to define pricing multipliers and crediting logic for internal simulation.

Phase 1 — Internal dogfood (4 weeks)
- Run platform internal tenants on new fidelity tiers. Collect metrics and tune rollback thresholds.
- Owner: product + applied ML.

Phase 2 — Opt-in customers (8–12 weeks)
- Invite 10–15 customers across sizes and verticals to opt-in. Run A/B experiments with controlled traffic percentages.
- Sales/GTM to provide commercial opt-in credits during experimentation.

Phase 3 — Gradual default exposure (6 months)
- Make adaptive tier available as default for new developer accounts with explicit consent and pricing disclosures.
- Expand tier availability across Dedicated clusters where capacity profiles match performance targets.

Phase 4 — Global rollout and pricing general availability
- G/A documentation, billing primitives, and long-term contracts update.

Pricing and packaging implications (table)

| Tier | Price multiplier | Typical latency band (P95) | Recommended use-cases |
| --- | ---: | --- | --- |
| Premium | x1.00 | <= 300ms | Production-critical low-latency transactional flows |
| Standard | x0.85 | <= 700ms | Most SaaS features, chat and content generation |
| Economy | x0.6 | <= 1.5s | Bulk generation, offline batch, high-throughput pipelines |
| Adaptive | variable | negotiated | Hybrid workloads — runtime chooses variant based on SLOs and cost targets |

(Implementation detail: multipliers are stored as per-customer configuration keys and applied at charge-time; for Dedicated contracts, multipliers can be overridden by contract SKU).

Observability and telemetry plan

- Required metrics: fidelity_tier, variant_id, request_id, customer_id, prompt_hash, quality_score_delta, tokens_consumed, latency_ms, fallback_triggered.
- Dashboards: per-tenant / global aggregation with retention 90 days by default (extended retention as paid add-on).
- Alert rules: quality_delta > 2.0 percentage points across canonical prompt-set (rolling 6h) -> SEV3; 4.0pp -> SEV2; 6.0pp and ongoing -> SEV1 + auto-rollback.

Quality evaluation and acceptance tests

- Canonical prompt-sets: curated per-vertical with ~500 prompts for primary languages supported. Maintained by applied ML with quarterly refresh.
- Acceptance run: every quantized or low-fidelity variant must pass nightly batch evaluation with acceptance thresholds defined per tier.

Developer and customer UX

- Console: fidelity selector, cost preview, latency estimate, sample outputs from chosen tier.
- API: headers to request fidelity overrides, plus per-response metadata identifying active variant and fallback reasons.
- Docs: migration guide and cheat sheet for choosing tiers.

Release notes and communications

- Release note draft for Phase 2 opt-in, Phase 3 default exposure, and Phase 4 GA. Each note includes: what changed, expected customer impact, rollback plan, and contact channels.
- GTM playbook: messaging templates for sales and success, opt-in crediting mechanics, and escalation contacts.

Open questions / decisions required

1. Exact multiplier values for per-tenant negotiated contracts (Finance input).
2. Retention policy for fidelity evaluation captures in regulated/customer-sensitive contexts (Legal & Security).
3. Compatibility and expectation matrix for on-prem/private deployments where hardware variability may require different fidelity defaults.

Appendix A — Example API snippets

- Request header to request a tier: 
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" -H "X-Redwood-Fidelity: standard" -d '{"input":"Summarize the following..."}'

- Response metadata sample: 
{"variant_id":"gpt-like-q3-std","fidelity_tier":"standard","fallback":"none","tokens":174} 

Appendix B — Rollout checklist (owner: product)

1. Acceptance prompt-set verified and signal dashboards green.
2. Billing multipliers configured in staging and validated with simulated invoices.
3. Canary automation configured (traffic targeting and rollback hooks).
4. GTM materials and support runbook published.
5. Legal & security sign-off on capture retention.

Summary

This consolidated governance blueprint balances product velocity with commercial discipline and safety. It creates a repeatable playbook for introducing fidelity as a measurable, monetizable product primitive while protecting customers from regressions. Next steps: finalize multiplier ranges (Finance), lock acceptance prompt-set (Applied ML), and begin Phase 0 workstreams in Q4 2026.
